models.name: Cloudflare Clef
models.config_equals_base: Yes for every architecture field: same as qwen38-27b (64 layers, 48 Gated DeltaNet + 16 full, 4 KV heads x 256). Only differences: mtp_num_hidden_layers 0 (MTP layer dropped), dtype/transformers_version, vision model_type string.
models.notes: Backbone = Qwen3.8-27B incl. vision tower; KV formula identical to qwen38-27b. HF safetensors.total 27,356,728,560 = qwen38-27b total minus the MTP layer; the separate joint_head.safetensors (0.256 GB bf16, ~0.13B params: width 1024, 2 routing + 4 layers, 16 heads, ffn 4096) is NOT in that total. Add ~0.26 GB for the head. Context: reference code default max_length 16,384 (mlx-community card: "the head was trained at 16k"); Workers AI serves 65,536 (model page, blog). Ollama tags advertise 256K (config max_position_embeddings) but that is not a validated decision length.

decision.output: Not next-token logits: a separate "joint schema head" (small transformer) reads the backbone final hidden states, routes evidence to each question and scores all options of ALL questions jointly in one forward pass; one logit per option, softmax per question. Question types noul / choice / score. Multiple questions per call: yes, up to 64 per request on Workers AI; llama.cpp README: "clef reads all the questions in one prompt and decides them jointly" (unlike other decision models, where each question is answered independently).
decision.typical_prompt_tokens: Cloudflare speed table uses ~800, ~3,400 and ~16,000-token requests (blog clef-faster-cheaper-multimodal). No single typical figure published.

max_options.source: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md (section POST /v1/systemone) ("255 for ... clef"); Cloudflare docs give no limit

official_formats.format: GGUF Q2_K..Q8_0, bf16 (bartowski, community; decision head kept at Q8_0, no imatrix possible)

runtimes.transformers: Yes, custom code: joint_schema_model.py (load_release_model, systemone()); tested torch 2.11 + transformers 5.10.2 on one H200 (card).
runtimes.sglang: Yes: Cloudflare serves Clef on SGLang; upstream in SGLang 0.5.22 (PR #42721); card gives docker lmsysorg/sglang:dev-clef with /v1/systemone (blog, card).
runtimes.vllm: Not listed: vLLM decision docs (2026-10-29 dev preview) list ClefFlashForJointSchema (clef-flash) and ClefOmniForJointSchema only, not the 27B.
runtimes.llama_cpp: Yes, native: arch "clef", PR #29831 merged 2026-10-03 (needs new llama_batch_ext decision-order API; single seq per batch; whole prompt must fit --ubatch-size). Text-only at merge; server README now lists clef among image-capable models. A server running clef serves only /v1/systemone (no text generation).
runtimes.ollama: Yes, local: Ollama >= 0.35.1 (library page "clef"), also :cloud tags.
runtimes.mlx: Only through mlx-community clef_mlx.py (runs backbone + joint head; one record per call, no batching). mlx_lm/mlx_vlm.generate and LM Studio load the backbone but output is meaningless (mlx-community card).
runtimes.plain_chat_runtimes: Not usable: needs the joint head; generic text generation gives meaningless output.

decision.benchmarks_claimed: Cloudflare (card, Decision Index 0.2.1 internal run): BANKING77 94.2, CLINC150+OOS 97.4, RAGTruth hallucination F1 79.4, MMLU 90.3; leads 7 of 10 decision benchmarks per changelog. mlx-community reports Cloudflare full-suite index 57.07 for clef-flash (not Clef). JevBench: not published by Cloudflare.

After SGLang move: ~800 tok 152 ms median; ~3,400 tok 305 ms; ~16,000 tok 1,635 ms (p95 1,805 ms)

throughput_published.derived_prefill_tok_s: ~9,800 tok/s at 16k, ~11,100 at 3.4k (tokens / median latency, one request)

models.name: OpenJev
models.config_equals_base: Yes: every architecture field equals qwen38-27b (config even keeps mtp_num_hidden_layers 1, but the safetensors total shows the MTP weights are not shipped). Diffs: dtype, transformers_version, vision rope fields.
models.notes: Plain causal LM (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration), no extra head: the decision is read from next-token logits of option letters, so KV/compute = qwen38-27b exactly. HF total 27,356,728,560. Base model not named in the main card (only "an Apache 2.0 open base model"); config/total identical to Qwen3.8-27B, and the Flash card calls it "OpenJev 27B". Card limits: prompts up to 16,384 tokens, one image per request. Cached-page latency shows prefix caching matters a lot.

decision.base_model: Not named in card (NOTICE file); architecture and param count identical to Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
decision.output: Options are lettered; the helper asks the server for ONE token and reads the logits of exactly those letters at the first output position, then applies fixed calibration (READOUT_T 0.85 etc.). One forward pass per question; several questions per API request (each its own pass, prefix-cached state). >52 options: groups of 52 then a final pass over winners.
decision.typical_prompt_tokens: ~1,460 tokens for a web decision with ~23 options (card).

max_options.source: card "Request limits"; llama.cpp README "52 for openjev"

official_formats.note: served with --quantization fp8 on one 80 GB GPU

runtimes.vllm: Yes, stock vLLM 0.29.0 + helper/shim.py (needs --max-logprobs 64, --served-model-name qwen, prefix caching); primary measured recipe. vLLM also has a generic NextTokenStrategy for Qwen3.5 on /v1/systemone.
runtimes.llama_cpp: Yes: native /v1/systemone since PR #29818 (merged 2026-10-02; vision too); or official GGUF via /completion n_probs (helper llama.cpp backend "on the list").
runtimes.plain_chat_runtimes: Works in principle (it is a normal LM: ask for the letter, max_tokens 4) but probabilities need top-k logprobs at position 1.

models.name: d3 (Decision 3.0, 27B)
models.config_equals_base: Yes: text architecture equals qwen38-27b (architectures Qwen3_5Model instead of ...ForConditionalGeneration, auto_map to modeling_d3.D3Model).
models.notes: Decision 3.0 (vLLM Semantic Router). Base model = Qwen3.5/3.8 weights loaded as Qwen3_5Model (no LM head: HF total excludes lm_head). Reads the prompt with BIDIRECTIONAL attention, so vLLM serves it without chunked prefill and without prefix caching; the whole prompt must fit one --ubatch in llama.cpp. Each question gets its own forward pass over the input (card), batched together. vLLM natively since PR #61565 (main, 2026-10-14; nightly, no release yet at card time); vLLM Semantic Router Engine mode; llama.cpp arch vllm-d3 (ggml-org GGUFs); Ollama library "d3" (27b/9b/4b/2b tags). KV note: with bidirectional attention and no prefix cache, KV for the prompt is only needed during the one prefill; the calculator should not assume cached-state reuse. max_context = card's recommended --max-model-len 32,768 ("plenty"; 32k-token text benchmarked); config allows 262,144.

decision.output: Answer-code readout: options get codes, probabilities = softmax of the options' code logits at the checkpoint temperature (vLLM docs). Multiple questions per call, "each from its own forward pass over the input" (card), batched.
decision.typical_prompt_tokens: ~330-token support ticket used for the speed table (card).

runtimes.vllm: Yes, native D3ForSequenceClassification (nightly; PR #61565), chunked prefill and prefix caching off.
runtimes.llama_cpp: Yes, arch vllm-d3 (whole prompt in one ubatch).

models.name: Perplexity pplx-decider v1.2 (27B)

models.name: Kev-27B (v2)
models.config_equals_base: Yes: text-only config (Qwen3_5TextModel, model_type qwen3_5_text) whose values equal qwen38-27b text_config; no vision tower.
models.notes: Full-weight fine-tune (v2) of Qwen3.8-27B, text only, LM head dropped (HF total 25,624,600,064) plus head.pt pointer head. Card: prefill-only causal backbone with a pointer head over the options; weights 51 GB, server ~65.5 GB resident; 64k state peaks 87.1 GB on H200. Smaller Kev sizes (0.8B/4B/9B) are LoRA adapters (see skipped).

decision.output: Pointer head over the option spans, single forward pass, calibrated probability per option; implements TypeSafe System One API. Each state is run once and its questions branch from it.

explainer.what_is_a_decision_model: A decision model is a language model used as a classifier: you send a situation (the "state": text, JSON, a web page or an image) plus typed questions with their allowed answers, and it returns a probability for every allowed option instead of writing text. The labels live in the request, so the same model routes a ticket, flags a policy breach or picks an agent's next click without retraining. The answer comes from a single prefill pass over the prompt (either the next-token scores of option letters, as in OpenJev, or a small head on the final hidden states, as in Clef), so there is no token-by-token generation and cost is input tokens only. Speed therefore depends on prefill throughput and prompt length, not on decode tokens per second.
calculator_implications: Work = one prefill of the whole prompt per request (Clef, pplx v1.2, d1: all questions in one pass) or per question (OpenJev, d3: one pass per question, state prefix-cached where the runtime allows; d3 is bidirectional so no prefix cache).

Decisions/s ~= prefill_tokens_per_s / prompt_tokens (x questions answered per pass). Published single-request points: Clef 27B ~9.8k tok/s at 16k (Workers AI/SGLang), OpenJev 27B FP8 ~8.6k tok/s at 15k (H100), d3 27B ~7.7k tok/s at 32k (MI325X), Kev-27B ~7k tok/s at 64k (H200), d3-flash 9B ~23.6k tok/s, d3-mini 4B ~31k tok/s, d1-3B ~33k tok/s on RTX 4090; Apple M5 Max MLX: Clef 27B 4-bit ~630 tok/s, Clef-flash 4-bit ~2.3k tok/s at 16k.
Memory = weights + KV/state for ONE prompt (no long generation), plus small heads (Clef ~0.12-0.26 GB).
Short prompts are latency-bound (fixed overhead ~20-80 ms on datacenter GPUs), so tok/s at 16-32k is the right figure for long states and per-request overhead dominates for 300-token tickets.
